M-O s.v. football: rugby, American football

harpastum, harpastī n.

noun, second declension

rugby; the ball

Classically harpastum is a small hard ball and the rough game played with it, in which the players snatched the ball from one another (Mart. 4.19.6, 7.67.4). “Play rugby” is harpastō lūdere (Traupman).

Other words

  • harpastum Britannicum

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. football: rugby: rugby

    Where it must be told apart from American football; Morgan–Owens also offers harpastum Rugbiēnse, after the school.
